findings.what: The implementer's forwardMerge fingerprint pair is not the reference's check, and its stated reason is wrong at this head.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 1: a role message the listener cannot deliver is kept outside the role lanes and forwarded once, in order, when a session claims the role; one release, and a listener of the previous release started against the new stream state still starts.
proof.surface: The envoy-listener binary built from this head, a real NATS server (internal/testnats/cmd/natsd) and a real session process, driven over the listener's HTTP API; then the previous release's listener built from the base this pull request now merges against, 0d71712bd594, on that same NATS and stream.
proof.observed: Three publishes to one unheld role each answered 202 {"kept":true,"kept_reason":"unclaimed"}; one POST /v1/roles/set delivered them at prompt lines 1, 2, 3 in publish order, each exactly once; a second claim of the same role added nothing (3 prompts before, 3 after). Rollback: the new listener left the stream subjects ["notifications.agent.>","notifications.dispatch.>","notifications.envoy.exceptions.notifications.agent.>","notifications.envoy.kept.>","notifications.ghostwispr.>","notifications.github.>","notifications.legion.>","notifications.slack.>","notifications.whatsapp.>"] and two kept messages; the previous-release binary then started on that state, logged `envoy-listener ready`, answered /healthz {"status":"healthy"} and left notifications.envoy.kept.> in place; when the new listener came back both kept messages still reached the role's next holder (2 of 2).
proof.negativeControl: The same unheld-role publish against that previous-release listener on the same live stack: HTTP 404 {"error":"no holder for role t-roll","reason":"unclaimed"}, and 404 again when the request carried keep:true, which that build does not read. On the deployed production listener, this session's own envoy_publish to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-839-nobody-holds-this was refused `no holder for role legion-infra-infra-839-nobody-holds-this`.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2: a kept message older than 1 hour when the role is claimed is not forwarded, and is dropped and counted.
proof.surface: The same live rig on a test build of this head whose keep window is shortened: a clone of 4f6e9985b979 under $TMPDIR with `const roleKeepWindow = 3 * time.Second` in place of `time.Hour` in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/role_keep.go and nothing else changed. Stated because an hour cannot be waited out: the age is the stream's own store time, which no caller chooses.
proof.observed: The publish was kept (202, event 68e8f06d889d12cab09f72c4c1fbe004); after 8 seconds the role was claimed; the holder was handed nothing for it; envoy_role_kept_expired_total moved 0 -> 1; the listener logged exactly one `listener dropped a kept role message older than the keep window` with topic notifications.role.t-stale, delivery_status expired, role t-stale, age 8.054424859s.
proof.negativeControl: The same run's three messages kept inside the shortened window, claimed at once, were all forwarded in order exactly once. So the drop is the age and not the build: one binary forwards what is young and drops what is old.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2: a forwarded kept message carries the time it was kept, so the holder can judge it.
proof.surface: The envelope on the holder's agent subject read from NATS, and the delivery card the agent itself reads — @legion/envoy-client's renderInbound, the function both plugins' delivery path calls.
proof.observed: Each of the three forwards on notifications.agent.ses_tester_rig carried kept_at (1793417096802, 1793417096896, 1793417097017) with topic notifications.role.t-order, while the stored copy on notifications.envoy.kept.role.t-order carried none, so the stamp is the forward's. renderInbound of such an envelope prints the agent's card with `kept_at: "2026-10-31T03:25:00Z"` beside `at:`.
proof.negativeControl: The rig fails closed on the copy that must not carry it: it refuses the run if the stored kept copy carries kept_at, and refuses it if any forward does not.
